  ## In the End
  
- This essay is somewhat of a commemoration. It has been 225 years (to the day the first excerpt of this essay was posted) since Davy’s Boxing Day Experiment with the first surgical anesthetic [^3]. Anesthesia was and remains closely associated with the terms and concepts such as altered states, inductions and depth. And these words so glibly used by hypnotists have a tangled history to them that goes back to the young days of science. It is 240 years since the Franklin Commission indicted Anton Mesmer’s animal magnetism to be a result of compression, imagination, and suggestion. 240 years also since Mesmer’s acolyte, Marquis de Puységur stumbled his way into the “magnetic sleep,” which perhaps was a link in the chain to the psychological turn of the Enlightenment [^4]. [The Age of Wonder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Age_of_Wonder) lies dead, and some may claim that science disinfects the mind of its magic in pinning it down to the material, Max Weber may say [disenchantment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disenchantment) has already won. [Trance should be dead](https://www.cosmic-pancakes.com/blog/barber-scientific?MerryXmasKev&Amy), but can we re-enchant the disenchanted? Because wonder is the first step to understanding, and beyond it lies Awe.

Language was important to him, in that time when there was little distinction between art, science, and philosophy. His experiments were public demonstrations in spectacle and intrigue. He was struck by the words his participants would use to describe their experience [^2]. They lacked the language then, and  theory too to describe this alteration in experience in this period that was called the [Age of Wonder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Age_of_Wonder). Two centuries later, can we do any better?

  ## In the End
  
- This essay is somewhat of a commemoration. It has been 225 years (to the day the first excerpt of this essay was posted) since Davy’s Boxing Day Experiment with the first surgical anesthetic [^3]. Anesthesia was and remains closely associated with the terms and concepts such as altered states, inductions and depth. And these words so glibly used by hypnotists have a tangled history to them that goes back to the young days of science. It is 240 years since the Franklin Commission indicted Anton Mesmer’s animal magnetism to be a result of compression, imagination, and suggestion. 240 years also since Mesmer’s acolyte, Marquis de Puységur stumbled his way into the “magnetic sleep,” which perhaps was a link in the chain to the psychological turn of the Enlightenment [^4]. [The Age of Wonder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Age_of_Wonder) lies dead, and some may claim that science disinfects the mind of its magic in pinning it down to the material, Max Weber may say [disenchantment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disenchantment) has already won. [Trance should be dead](https://www.cosmic-pancakes.com/blog/barber-scientific?MerryXmasKev&Amy), but can we re-enchant the disenchanted? Because wonder is the first step to understanding, and beyond it lies Awe.

Based on the papers you've provided, here's a suggested citation note for [^7] that ties together the Dynamic Framework of Thought (DFT) literature:

The DFT was first proposed in Christoff et al. (2016) "Mind-wandering as spontaneous thought: a dynamic framework" as a way to understand spontaneous thought. The framework has since been extended to understand flow states (Shepherd, 2022), creativity and psychedelic states (Girn et al., 2020), and has found empirical support in studies of thought dynamics (Nakatani et al., 2019). Together these works suggest that the constraints on thought can help us understand different states of mind, from focused flow to creative insights to psychedelic experiences.

This captures the key papers while showing how the framework has evolved from its original conception to broader applications in understanding different mental states, which fits well with how you're using it in the essay. Would you like me to suggest any adjustments to this citation note?
